goal: Standardize pricing-service on a test framework for its Python test suite going forward, keeping the suite runnable in CI as the service evolves.
question: Select the test framework that pricing-service should standardize on for its Python test suite going forward.
known_constraints: The suite runs in GitHub Actions CI (ubuntu-latest) via an editable install of the dev extra followed by a single test command.
evidence: pytest>=8 is the declared dev dependency (pyproject.toml, [project.optional-dependencies].dev)
the only test module imports pytest and uses @pytest.mark.parametrize (tests/test_pricing.py:1,6)
README states all tests run under pytest in CI and that the suite and onboarding docs assume pytest (README.md:3-4)
a repo-wide search found no references to unittest, nose, nose2, hypothesis, tox, or coverage (rg search, 2026-10-02)
runtime dependencies are empty; only dev tooling adds a dependency (pyproject.toml:5)
the suite consists of one module with one parametrized test covering tier_price (tests/test_pricing.py)
no external documentation was reachable in this session, so upstream release cadence and Python-version support of third-party options were not verified

alternatives.name: Keep pytest
alternatives.description: Continue using pytest>=8 as the test framework, with the existing test module, dev dependency, and CI invocation unchanged.
advantages: The existing test module, CI job, and dev dependency already target pytest, so nothing needs to change
Supports parametrized tests, which the current suite uses
README and onboarding docs already describe the suite as pytest-based
disadvantages: Retains a third-party dev dependency that must be tracked for upgrades
Any future move away from pytest would still require rewriting the suite and CI
assumptions: Keeping a third-party dev dependency is acceptable to the team

alternatives.name: Standard-library unittest
alternatives.description: Migrate the test module to Python's built-in unittest module and remove the pytest dev dependency.
advantages: Requires no third-party test dependency because unittest ships with Python
Runs with the standard-library unittest runner, so CI needs only the project install
Standard-library API is stable across supported Python versions
disadvantages: The existing pytest-style test must be rewritten (for example replacing @pytest.mark.parametrize with subTest)
The CI command, dev extra, and the README's pytest assumptions would all need updating
Assertions and test organization are more verbose than the current suite
assumptions: Removing the third-party dev dependency is worth the migration effort

alternatives.name: nose2
alternatives.description: Adopt nose2, a unittest-compatible test runner with a plugin architecture, and rewrite the test module for it.
advantages: Builds on unittest-style tests while adding plugin-based features
Offers plugin integration such as coverage reporting
disadvantages: Adds a third-party dependency whose release cadence is not documented in this repository
The existing pytest-style test must be rewritten and CI and docs updated
Provides no capability the current suite's single parametrized test requires
assumptions: nose2 remains installable and compatible with the project's supported Python versions (not verified in this session)
